reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses sintering inhomogeneity and phase formation in high-entropy alloys, but neither addresses vapor-phase copper coating of tungsten, its effect on oxides or wettability, or W–Cu composite properties. The key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: Vapor-phase copper coating can be uniformly applied to tungsten particles
The coating reduces native oxide barriers and improves wettability
Improved wettability and oxide removal enhance interfacial bonding during sintering
Enhanced bonding reduces voids and phase separation in W–Cu composites
Reduced defects improve thermal conductivity and mechanical durability under irradiation
